newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fanuc sees 1997/98 profit rising by 2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Fanuc sees 1997/98 profit rising by 2 pct.

text.p: Japan's Fanuc Ltd said on Friday its parent current profit would increase to 47.7 billion yen in the year to March 31, 1998, up two percent from the estimated current profit for the previous year.
Fanuc, one of the world's leading producers of machine tools, now expects its parent current profit for the year to March 31, 1997, to be 46.8 billion yen, a company spokesman said.
He added that, if profits rise in 1997/98, it would be the fourth year in a row of profit growth, which has been fuelled by strong sales of industrial robots.
"Sales of plastic-injection molding machines are up both in the domestic and foreign markets," he added.
Profit growth, however, would slow from previous years because of the high cost of acquiring materials for parts, due to the weak yen, the Fanuc spokesman said.
Fanuc said its parent sales in 1997/98 are expected to grow to 170 billion yen, up nine percent from its estimate for 1996/97.
Fanuc said that its group net profit in 1996/97 would grow to 30.6 billion yen, up 18 percent from the year before.
Profits have been rising at its overseas sales subsidiaries in Europe and the United States due to increasing demand, the spokesman added.
